# [B1 — Combined sewer overflow](../hypodrafts/B1.md "Combined sewer overflow")

*Generated by `scripts/pages/hypodraft_b1.py`: what the data held here, and the public records named, can and cannot show about the hypothesis. Each marked statement links to what it rests on.*

**Draft, not a result.** <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-STATUS">The test this page specifies has not been run: no script in this repository fetches the bathing-water samples, joins a rain series to them, or computes either consequence.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-STATUS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The observable consequence

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-VOLUME">[B1](../hypodrafts/B1.md "Combined sewer overflow") is to be discriminated *against per-outfall discharge volume*. That volume is reported to PULS at one of the knowledge levels Miljøstyrelsen's DP02 sets, from a PULS calculation to measurement-based estimation, and how many structures report a measured volume is not known here; below the measured level it is a model output driven by rainfall, which drives every rival too, so regressing a rainfall-driven response on it tests rainfall.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-VOLUME "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-HALF">This draft takes a **weaker, falsifiable half**: combined systems deliver *raw sewage* to the shore, event-timed, on a schedule set by their own storage. Two consequences follow, neither using a modelled volume.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-HALF "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-C1">**`C1` — the class contrast.** At bathing sites whose nearest rain-conditioned outfall is **combined** (`OV/OS/OF/OK/Bypass`), the faecal-indicator response to antecedent rainfall is **steeper** than where the nearest is **separate** stormwater (`SE/SF`), at equal distance, region, month and rainfall.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-C1 "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-TYPETAL">The typetal in DP02 put total nitrogen at [12](../SOURCES.md#F-ed9b66fb2e) mg/l in overflow water and [43](../SOURCES.md#F-ed9b66fb2e) mg/l in sewage, against [2](../SOURCES.md#F-dc7ebb6bb1) mg/l at a separate system's stormwater outlet.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-TYPETAL "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-SEWAGE">Overflow water carries sewage and separate stormwater is meant to carry none, so a faecal indicator should rise more with rain where the nearest outfall is combined — though runoff can bring animal faeces into both arms.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-SEWAGE "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-C1-FALSIFY">*Falsified if the class × rain interaction is inside the null below, or negative.* [B2](../HYPOTHESES.md "Separate stormwater") alone predicts a rain main effect in **both** arms and a null interaction — so this is the [B1](../hypodrafts/B1.md "Combined sewer overflow")/[B2](../HYPOTHESES.md "Separate stormwater") discrimination.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-C1-FALSIFY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-C2">**`C2` — the storage kink.** A combined structure spills once rain exceeds what it stores. `(vol_sb + vol_fbas)` over `Red areal` gives a **critical rainfall depth in mm** per structure, from engineering attributes that do not move with the weather. [B1](../hypodrafts/B1.md "Combined sewer overflow") predicts a **kink** at that site-specific, *a-priori* depth, with no free breakpoint. *Falsified if the kink amplitude at each site's own threshold sits inside the null from permuting thresholds.*</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-C2 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-CONFOUND">**How the shared-rainfall confound breaks.** Rainfall enters both arms of `C1` identically and cancels in the contrast. In `C2` the *location* of the threshold is the signal, and it varies for reasons the weather does not know: runoff, riverine particulate organic carbon, buoyancy, resuspension and bather density are all smooth in rainfall and none carries a basin volume. No modelled overflow volume enters either statistic.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-CONFOUND "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The data, counted here

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-TAXONOMY">Error classes are those of [a taxonomy that rates a data stream by the errors it can contain](https://github.com/Jjokulian/statistical-methods#7b-rate-a-data-stream-by-the-errors-it-can-contain): `2` is quantisation, among it censoring at a threshold; `4` schema conflation, one column pooling incommensurables; `6` an absent dimension, no column at all; `7` model-as-datum, a modelled value in a column shaped like a measured one.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-TAXONOMY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-WISE">**Bathing-water samples.** The EEA's WISE table `timeseries_MonitoringResult`, queried through `discodata.eea.europa.eu/sql`, holds [172,440](../SOURCES.md#F-7c289101d6) Danish samples, each dated and each with an E. coli and an enterococci count, under [1,437](../SOURCES.md#F-7c289101d6) site identifiers over the seasons [2008](../SOURCES.md#F-7c289101d6)–[2024](../SOURCES.md#F-7c289101d6): [10,144](../SOURCES.md#F-efa7bb374e) a season on average. No count is empty. E. coli is flagged at the limit of detection on [26,301](../SOURCES.md#F-3bda9a7c2e) samples and as a missing value on [688](../SOURCES.md#F-f26642c9d0) that still carry a number (enterococci: [31,478](../SOURCES.md#F-110c2bc73a) and [723](../SOURCES.md#F-6cc573ab3d)). A record has a sample date and no time of day.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-WISE "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-WISE-CLASS">The detection-limit flag is censoring, class `2`: boundable, not recoverable. The missing time of day is class `6`, an absent dimension, which no processing can restore.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-WISE-CLASS "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-PERIODS">**The dated episode log**, `timeseries_SeasonalPeriod`, holds for Danish sites [1,208](../SOURCES.md#F-d0be24a951) `shortTermPollution` periods ([2011](../SOURCES.md#F-d0be24a951)–[2024](../SOURCES.md#F-d0be24a951)), [755](../SOURCES.md#F-40c3aa9dbd) `bathingProhibition` (from [2017](../SOURCES.md#F-40c3aa9dbd)), [76](../SOURCES.md#F-7611cfd1db) `abnormalSituation` and [76](../SOURCES.md#F-7eaf026628) `cyanobacteriaBloom` periods.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-PERIODS "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-FLAGS">**Sample flags** over the same samples: [1,272](../SOURCES.md#F-e76871adf0) `shortTermPollutionSample`, [1,205](../SOURCES.md#F-8a1720e716) `replacementSample`, [22,912](../SOURCES.md#F-69e9eee4c9) `preSeasonSample`. The table keeps all of them; which of them a compliance assessment may set aside is the Directive's rule, which was not read here.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-FLAGS "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-LAYER">**Bathing sites.** `data/raw/national/badevand.geojson` holds [1,026](../SOURCES.md#F-aee9bd61e1) sites with latitude, longitude and a `DKBW…` identifier, and every one of its identifiers is among the Danish identifiers of the EEA table. The table holds more — [1,437](../SOURCES.md#F-7c289101d6) with samples, [1,049](../SOURCES.md#F-24bac07e31) of them never marked delisted — so delisting does not account for all of the difference.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-LAYER "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-CSO">**Combined overflows.** `data/raw/spildevand/combined_overflow.geojson` holds [4,217](../SOURCES.md#F-07fbaf3991) structures with `Red areal`, an annual volume and `Antal overløb`; `Antal overløb` is empty for [1,676](../SOURCES.md#F-6f6cbc74df) of them ([39.7](../SOURCES.md#F-c83c2fdb24)%), the volume empty for [77](../SOURCES.md#F-982983a967) and zero for [719](../SOURCES.md#F-09502dc1d5).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-CSO "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-CSO-VOLUME">The annual volume is modelled wherever it is not measured — class `7` there — and is not used here.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-CSO-VOLUME "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-RBU">**The national register** `data/raw/national/punkt_rbu_udl.geojson` holds [19,665](../SOURCES.md#F-1dcf8ae5fb) rain-conditioned outfall points: `vol_sb` is filled on [4,068](../SOURCES.md#F-cdfe45be35) ([2,740](../SOURCES.md#F-423945a5f6) of them zero), `vol_fbas` on [8,763](../SOURCES.md#F-e9e1c0bbb1) ([5,771](../SOURCES.md#F-817691b695) zero).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-RBU "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-JOIN">**The two together.** [3,712](../SOURCES.md#F-36be190051) of [4,130](../SOURCES.md#F-61c5fecd1b) distinct overflow names equal a register `pkt_navn`. The two files disagree on how many structures there are of a type — `OV` [2,812](../SOURCES.md#F-cb1fe19ee6) against [3,015](../SOURCES.md#F-2e266d7555), `OF` [77](../SOURCES.md#F-8a40aaf388) against [209](../SOURCES.md#F-0d072adc95) — and both carry type codes that are not among DP02's structure codes: `UR`, `OVI`, `OSI` and `OKI`, and in the register `ikke oplyst`.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-JOIN "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-JOIN-CLASS">A code outside DP02's lists is a column holding what its schema does not define: class `4`, not boundable from inside the files.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-JOIN-CLASS "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-DEPTH">**Derived here: critical rainfall depth.** [1,066](../SOURCES.md#F-e014f46298) overflows have a name matching exactly one register point, positive storage and positive reduced area; their depth is [0.42](../SOURCES.md#F-f0a6a6d29e) mm at the tenth percentile, [5.2](../SOURCES.md#F-ee22141abc) mm at the median, [32.5](../SOURCES.md#F-940d0af95c) mm at the ninetieth and [2,670](../SOURCES.md#F-cec2c94a97) mm at the most.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-DEPTH "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-TAIL">A basin that stores [2,670](../SOURCES.md#F-cec2c94a97) mm of rain over its reduced area is implausible, so the tail is taken as a unit error and trimmed above the `p95`.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-TAIL "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-NEAREST">**Derived here: the nearest outfall.** Of the [1,026](../SOURCES.md#F-aee9bd61e1) bathing sites, [284](../SOURCES.md#F-7c269aca21) have a combined structure nearest and [742](../SOURCES.md#F-a686828d58) a separate outlet; the median distance is [0.87](../SOURCES.md#F-605657cf41) km, [541](../SOURCES.md#F-61ea936278) lie within a kilometre (`within_1km`) and [741](../SOURCES.md#F-e87c84eae8) within two (`within_2km`).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-NEAREST "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-RAIN">**Rainfall is the gap.** No rain-gauge series is held. The rain record held, under `data/raw/weather`, is hourly ERA5 reanalysis over Copenhagen from Open-Meteo, and the Baltic winds under `data/raw/marine` are ERA5 too; a reanalysis in place of gauges would be class `7`.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-RAIN "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-DMI">DMI's metObs API serves station precipitation at ten-minute and hourly steps (`precip_past10min`, `precip_past1h`); the source register records test queries answered with no API key, contradicting older documentation, and says to confirm the key policy before building on it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-DMI "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Other sources, and whether each is a production path separate from modelled volume.** <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-NONATIONAL">No national series of measured overflow is held or was found here: the public extract carries each structure's reported annual volume and number of overflows, and how many of those volumes were measured is not known.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-NONATIONAL "What this claim rests on")</sup>

- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-SRC-WISE">**WISE bathing water** (above) — **a separate path**: counts per dated sample and the periods authorities report, with no hydraulic model in the chain.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-SRC-WISE "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-SRC-VHF">**Vesthimmerlands Forsyning** (`/spildevand/overloebsdata`) publishes, for the [11](../SOURCES.md#F-448c8de4d5) registered overflow points on its combined systems, monthly counts and volumes of overflow for 2025 with an archive of earlier years; the points carry sensors that measure overflow, and some discharge to the Limfjord.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-SRC-VHF "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-SRC-VHF-LEVEL">So a measured set, but a small one — and whether its volumes meet DP02's measurement-based level, whose examples add measured substance to measured flow, the page does not say.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-SRC-VHF-LEVEL "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-SRC-KBH">**Copenhagen's bathing-water forecast** — whether it keeps a public archive of measured overflow is not established: its host `kbh.badevand.dk` did not resolve from here.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-SRC-KBH "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The null, under the constraint imposed

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-CLUSTER">The nominal null for [172,440](../SOURCES.md#F-7c289101d6) samples is wrong: sampling is day-clustered. Over the seasons 2011–2024 the table's [130,773](../SOURCES.md#F-24e2437853) Danish samples fall on [1,425](../SOURCES.md#F-24e2437853) distinct dates, [92](../SOURCES.md#F-421a6a91f5) per date and [102](../SOURCES.md#F-421a6a91f5) sampling days a season. Weather is common within a day and correlated across the country, so the independent unit is the **site-day cluster**, and even those dates are not independent draws on weather.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-CLUSTER "What this claim rests on")</sup>

- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-N1">**`N1` (primary, `C1`): permute the class label** across sites within strata of (distance decile × region × outfall count within [2](../SOURCES.md#F-0198bef2c4) km), [10,000](../SOURCES.md#F-d9a0178833) draws — destroys the combined/separate contrast, preserves rainfall, geography, season and site baselines.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-N1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-N2">**`N2` (`C1`): circular shift of the daily rainfall field by whole years**, [16](../SOURCES.md#F-1dc6b55e39) non-zero shifts over the seasons [2008](../SOURCES.md#F-7c289101d6)–[2024](../SOURCES.md#F-7c289101d6), preserving seasonality, day-clustering and autocorrelation. **The smallest attainable p is one in [17](../SOURCES.md#F-9dcb6c64f6), [0.059](../SOURCES.md#F-bb13d681e9) — state it, never exceed it.** Report the more conservative of `N1` and `N2`.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-N2 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-N3">**`N3` (`C2`): permute the predicted threshold** across structures within a spill-volume stratum: keeps the kink, destroys the link to a site's own storage.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-N3 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-CENSOR">**Left-censoring is not small**: [26,301](../SOURCES.md#F-3bda9a7c2e) of [172,440](../SOURCES.md#F-7c289101d6) E. coli values sit at the limit of detection ([15.3](../SOURCES.md#F-cbc71b0ba9)%). Fit a censored-normal on log10 counts; a substitution rule invents the effect.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-CENSOR "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-POSITIONS">**Sites are positions, not replicates**, never aggregated into water bodies: the unit is outfall-to-site distance, which is what the mechanism has.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-POSITIONS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## Procedure

1. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-P1">Stream the Danish subset of `timeseries_MonitoringResult` and `timeseries_SeasonalPeriod` from DISCODATA; join to `badevand.geojson` on its `DKBW…` identifiers.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-P1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
2. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-P2">Per site: nearest combined and nearest separate register point, and counts within [500](../SOURCES.md#F-7cb01d25a1) m, [1](../SOURCES.md#F-66ae7ffc27) km and [2](../SOURCES.md#F-0198bef2c4) km. Keep the geometry; aggregate nothing.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-P2 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
3. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-P3">Rainfall: confirm DMI's key policy, then antecedent depth over [6](../SOURCES.md#F-6bcd3e1197), [12](../SOURCES.md#F-b546658ccf), [24](../SOURCES.md#F-cae6670ef6) and [48](../SOURCES.md#F-b5ffbe35ae) h before each sample at the nearest gauge. Until then the design is stated, not run.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-P3 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
4. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-P4">**`C1`:** censored regression of log10 E. coli on rain × class, with site fixed effects, month, distance and year. Report the interaction. Repeat on enterococci — a second organism, not a second dataset.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-P4 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
5. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-P5">**`C2`:** for the [1,066](../SOURCES.md#F-e014f46298) threshold-bearing structures and their nearest sites, test the jump at each site's own predicted depth, standardised and summed across sites.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-P5 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
6. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-P6">**Anchor:** samples inside a declared `shortTermPollution` period against matched samples at the same site and month outside one — the arm that uses no rain model at all.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-P6 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
7. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-P7">Null under `N1`, `N2` and `N3`.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-P7 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## What a result would and would not license

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-WOULD">**Would.** That combined systems deliver sewage-borne contamination to the shore, event-timed, near their outfalls, across [17](../SOURCES.md#F-9dcb6c64f6) seasons and [1,026](../SOURCES.md#F-aee9bd61e1) sites — and via `C2` that the timing is set by storage, not weather alone. It separates [B1](../hypodrafts/B1.md "Combined sewer overflow") from [B2](../HYPOTHESES.md "Separate stormwater") on a signature rather than a shared driver.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-WOULD "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Would not.** <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-NOT-OXYGEN">(a) **Nothing about oxygen.** This is [B1](../hypodrafts/B1.md "Combined sewer overflow")'s delivery limb, bearing on [O9](../HYPOTHESES.md "Bathing water failure"), not on [O1](../HYPOTHESES.md "Oxygen deficit"): faecal indicators are not COD, so the oxygen claim stays unscored — and they are not the rotting algae that fedtemøg names, so [O2](../HYPOTHESES.md "Fedtemøg") stays unscored too.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-NOT-OXYGEN "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-NOT-LOAD">(b) No load, no volume, no attribution — there is no denominator, so any *share of* is out of reach by construction.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-NOT-LOAD "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-NOT-WINDOW">(c) The window is **bathing season only**, set by human use and so circular, as [NITROGEN.md](../NITROGEN.md) argues.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-NOT-WINDOW "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-NOT-SELECTED">(d) Sampling may be **selected against the exposure** — if visits avoid storms, and since the table flags replacement samples beside short-term-pollution ones — which would attenuate the effect toward zero, so a positive result survives it but a null does **not** license *no effect*.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-NOT-SELECTED "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-NOT-TWO">(e) E. coli and enterococci are two counts from one sample and one visit: one piece of evidence, not two.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-BA-B1-NOT-TWO "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-BA-B1-IMPROVE">**Smallest improvement:** the per-structure knowledge level from PULS, or a measured-overflow record such as Vesthimmerlands Forsyning publishes.
